title: Korea Quantum Computing (KQC) to Go Public on Nasdaq via $80 Million SPAC Merger with Charlton Aria - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Korea Quantum Computing’s parent KQC Quantum is going public on Nasdaq via an $80M pre-money SPAC merger with Charlton Aria (CHAR), implying roughly $215M pro forma equity value and a $30M minimum-cash condition, expected to close in 1H 2027. It sells hardware-agnostic quantum middleware (Qubiteer) and PQC security tools.

insights.claim: KQC Quantum signed a definitive business combination agreement with Charlton Aria Acquisition Corp (NASDAQ: CHAR) at an $80 million pre-money equity value ($11.00 per share), implying about $215 million pro forma equity value, with closing expected in the first half of 2027 under the ticker 'KQC'.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Another quantum SPAC listing; compare valuation against other small-cap quantum names.

insights.claim: Charlton Aria’s trust holds about $93.5 million as of September 2026, the deal has a $30 million minimum cash closing condition, and existing KQC shareholders roll over 100% of equity (owning roughly 37% to 47% pro forma).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The gap between trust size and the $30M minimum implies redemptions are expected; closing risk depends on how many trust holders redeem.

insights.claim: Net proceeds will fund Qubiteer engineering, QuantumSpan deployment, KCMVP security certifications and conversion of enterprise pilots into full commercial deployments in South Korea and Southeast Asia.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Use of proceeds is about commercialization of pilots, so watch pilot-to-contract conversion post-listing.

insights.claim: KQC, founded in Busan in 2021, is a hardware-agnostic quantum middleware and post-quantum security integrator rather than a hardware builder.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An asset-light software model avoids hardware capex but depends on third-party QPU access.

insights.claim: Its flagship Qubiteer platform, in beta since June 2026, is an AI-driven hybrid engine that converts business constraints into mathematical models and dispatches workloads to classical, annealing or gate-model QPUs, including D-Wave Leap cloud access.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Qubiteer depends on D-Wave cloud access, tying KQC’s prospects to third-party hardware.
insights.locator: The company is engineering its flagship software platform

insights.claim: Named customer engagements include battery cathode optimization with POSCO, urban rail scheduling with Busan Transit, and paid PQC migration proofs-of-concept with Industrial Bank of Korea and LS ITC.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Pilots and proofs-of-concept, not yet large recurring contracts; revenue scale remains unproven.

insights.claim: KQC also sells hardware security modules and is developing QuantumSpan, a platform to audit cryptographic assets and manage PQC migration across enterprise networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: PQC migration tooling is the nearer-term revenue line versus quantum optimization.
